KEY MESSAGE 1...A Noreaster will continue to impact at least 
Downeast Maine into Tuesday AM, bringing breezy winds, high 
surf, and periods of rain.

KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...
The center of low associated with this Noreaster continues to 
drift NW this afternoon now located along the southern New 
Jersey coast. A large occlusion is wrapped up just south of Cape
Cod with a triple point near Georges Bank. Satellite imagery is
showing moisture advecting north in Maine from the the Atlantic
which extends back to the Bahamas. This has increased PWATs 
over Downeast Maine into the 175-200 percent of normal range for
late September. At the same time a strong 1028mb high pressure 
system sits over Central Quebec with a 584dam 500mb ridge. The 
placement of the ridge and North Atlantic low pressure near 
Greenland is preventing this Noreaster from moving and nearly 
cutoff from the flow. 

Throughout this afternoon expect the Noreaster low pressure to 
drift closer to NYC as surface high drifts into the Maritimes. 
This will result in lessening precip chances across the CWA 
through this afternoon. Tonight, the 500mb ridge will fold over
and shift out over the North Atlantic which will allow the 
upper level low of this Noreaster to lift back into the mid 
latitude westerlies. This will begin to push the surface low 
northward into Southern New England as it slowly begins to 
weaken. The northerly movement will allow for increasing POPs 
across the entire CWA late tonight into Monday and lasting into
Tuesday with periods of rain expected. Overall, the wind field 
will weaken as the sfc low pressure lifts N then NE across the 
Gulf of Maine. Then by Tuesday afternoon the system will be 
exiting east across Nova Scotia. Here is what to expect for the 
various components of the storm:

Periods of Rain...Lingering rain chances Downeast and across the
Bangor region this afternoon and early evening, then areawide 
increasing POPs tonight lasting into Tuesday AM. Although there 
remains significant uncertainty how many periods of rain
develop, the overall trend for slightly lower values has 
persisted into this afternoon. However, with PWATs areawide 
eventually up to around 190 percent of normal we can expect some
beneficial rainfall. The best beneficial rainfall will be 
across the Bangor Region to far Southern Aroostook County and 
points southward to the Downeast coast. It is here that 0.6-1 
inch is expected for totals, north of here significant 
uncertainty exists due to dry air, totals in northern areas 
generally 0.1-0.3 inch. We do not expect any flooding concerns 
anywhere given the D1-D3 drought conditions. In fact nearly all 
of the rainfall will likely be absorbed into the near surface 
ground and very unlikely any water gets into the rivers and 
streams. Rivers and streams are currently in the 1-15th 
percentile range with many approaching top 5 lowest flows on 
record. 

Breezy Winds...Winds from the northeast will be the gustiest 
through Monday AM and begin to weaken into the afternoon and
Monday night. Winds will be stronger the further south you go 
but will top out around 25 mph across Bangor and the Downeast 
with the system remaining so far south of the CWA. Isolated 
higher gusts possible especially near the Downeast coastline
exposed to the NE winds across the open waters. We don't 
anticipate impacts from the wind other than maybe a very few
isolated power outages Downeast.

High Surf...Seas near the shore will be fairly rough with 4-8 
ft seas, much of it as a longer period south/southeast swell. We
are not expecting impactful coastal flooding, though waves 
breaking on the rocks will be hazardous for any onlookers. 
Conditions should be a bit more hazardous for coastal Hancock 
than coastal Washington. Conditions slowly ease tonight into 
Monday.
